sections.title: باب 6 — متن (6)

paras.text: … constitutions are nominal or formal are not respected, and in a civilised society the survival of such parties is impossible. The constitution is the means of the distribution of powers within the party, and in the party leadership powers are distributed grade by grade. Parties take part in elections in the light of a manifesto. Party participation in elections becomes the cause of improvement and transparency of the electoral system, because parties keep an eye on the electoral system.

paras.text: Political parties without members are like a hollow body. A political party prepares a programme and conveys it to the public. If there is effect in this programme, people start taking interest in it and obtain membership of that political party. This membership is voluntary and they are not given any kind of salary; rather, to run party affairs, these same volunteers give donations from their own pockets. These volunteers follow the instructions of the leadership. These people with great zeal and passion try to spread the programme and ideology of their party among the public so that party membership increases. Members elect the leadership. These same volunteers take part actively in elections, meetings, processions and demonstrations etc. These volunteers of the party offer every kind of sacrifice for their party. Membership is given according to the constitution of the party. The membership of a volunteer can be suspended when he violates the manifesto and constitution of the party. The success of parties depends on active members (Activists). Collecting the greatest number of volunteer members depends on the character of the party, the learning and personality of the leadership and the party manifesto. If the party programme mirrors the psychology and trends of the citizens of that country and the party’s means of communication are effective, then the greatest number of people will join the party. The uniformity of ideology among the volunteers and the struggle for the ideology become the cause of party unity. The party remains organised and the volunteers play a key and critical role in elections.

… constitutions are nominal or formal are not respected, and in a civilised society the survival of such parties is impossible. The constitution is the means of the distribution of powers within the party, and in the party leadership powers are distributed grade by grade. Parties take part in elections in the light of a manifesto. Party participation in elections becomes the cause of improvement and transparency of the electoral system, because parties keep an eye on the electoral system.

3. Volunteers:

Political parties without members are like a hollow body. A political party prepares a programme and conveys it to the public. If there is effect in this programme, people start taking interest in it and obtain membership of that political party. This membership is voluntary and they are not given any kind of salary; rather, to run party affairs, these same volunteers give donations from their own pockets. These volunteers follow the instructions of the leadership. These people with great zeal and passion try to spread the programme and ideology of their party among the public so that party membership increases. Members elect the leadership. These same volunteers take part actively in elections, meetings, processions and demonstrations etc. These volunteers of the party offer every kind of sacrifice for their party. Membership is given according to the constitution of the party. The membership of a volunteer can be suspended when he violates the manifesto and constitution of the party. The success of parties depends on active members (Activists). Collecting the greatest number of volunteer members depends on the character of the party, the learning and personality of the leadership and the party manifesto. If the party programme mirrors the psychology and trends of the citizens of that country and the party’s means of communication are effective, then the greatest number of people will join the party. The uniformity of ideology among the volunteers and the struggle for the ideology become the cause of party unity. The party remains organised and the volunteers play a key and critical role in elections.

4. Leadership:

No organised human group is complete without leadership. Political parties are organised groups and they run through elected leadership. Leadership is always personalities well known at the national level who have political experience and are far-sighted. A leader is always intelligent and aware of national problems. Sometimes the leadership has to face great difficulties. It is made the target of vindictive actions and violence. The success of any political party depends mostly on the leadership. ۴۔ قیادت:

sections.title: باب 6 — متن (7)

paras.text: … observe the leadership and test its character, and then allocate a place for that party in national politics. People note every word of the leader and comment on it. paras.text: Government of a Political Party and its Performance in the light of its Manifesto
paras.urdu: سیاسی جماعت کی حکومت کا اُسکے منشور کی روشنی میں کارکردگی (Government of a Political Party and its Performance in the light of its Manifesto)
paras.pashto: د سیاسي ګوند حکومت او د هغه د منشور په رڼا کې کړنې

paras.text: A necessary element of every political party is the party’s manifesto (Charter/Manifesto). Every political party, identifying the important problems of the country, compiles a programme or proposals to solve those problems, which is called a manifesto. In the light of this same manifesto, in the form of political and electoral promises, parties take part in elections. When the majority of the public agree with these promises and programmes, that party, winning the elections (obtaining the public mandate), forms the government. Here it is worth mentioning that the vote should always be given by looking at the manifesto or programme of a party. When the majority party forms the government, it then makes laws to give practical form to its promises and manifesto. To solve problems the party changes its proposals into law. In the developed world this is the method, because of which the political systems there are stable. Our problem is that parties, on coming into power, ignore their manifesto and programme, and a negative political culture comes into being. The result is that our political system remains unstable.

مشاہدہ کرتے ہیں اور اِس کا کردار جانچتے ہیں اور پھر اُس پارٹی کیلئے قومی سیاست میں جگہ مختص کرتے ہیں۔ لوگ قائد کی ہر بات نوٹ کرتے ہیں اور اِس پر تبصرہ کرتے ہیں۔ کسی بھی سیاسی جماعت میں اہم ترین عہدے چیئرمین، صدر، جنرل سیکرٹری، پریس سیکرٹری، فنانس سیکرٹری وغیرہ کے ہوتے ہیں۔ اِن کے درمیان اِختیارات کی باقاعدہ تقسیم ہوتی ہے۔

اگر سیاسی جماعتیں اُصولوں اور قاعدوں کی بنیاد پر بنائی گئی ہوں تو پھر یہ جماعتیں جمہوریت کی روح ثابت ہوتی ہیں۔ اِن کی سوچ تعمیری اور تخلیقی ہوتی ہے۔ آئین میں تقسیمِ اِختیارات کو قومی مفادات کی روشنی میں دیکھتی ہیں۔ یہی جماعتیں جماعتی اِتحاد کی ترقی کا باعث بنتی ہیں اور اِنتخابی نظام کی اہمیت پر یقین یا اعتماد رکھتی ہیں جو کہ ایک کامیاب سیاسی نظام کا پیش خیمہ ثابت ہوتا ہے۔

سیاسی جماعت کی حکومت کا اُسکے منشور کی روشنی میں کارکردگی (Government of a Political Party and its Performance in the light of its Manifesto)

ہر سیاسی جماعت کا ایک لازمی عنصر جماعت کا منشور (Charter/Manifesto) ہے۔ ہر سیاسی جماعت ملک کے اہم مسائل کی نشاندہی کر کے اُن مسائل کو حل کرنے کیلئے پروگرام یا تجاویز مرتب کرتی ہے جسے منشور کہا جاتا ہے۔ اِسی منشور کی روشنی میں سیاسی و اِنتخابی وعدوں کی شکل میں جماعتیں اِنتخابات میں حصہ لیتی ہیں۔ جب عوام کی اکثریت اِن وعدوں اور پروگراموں سے متفق ہو تو وہ جماعت اِنتخابات جیت کر (عوامی مینڈیٹ حاصل کر کے) حکومت بناتی ہے۔ یہاں یہ بات قابلِ ذکر ہے کہ ووٹ ہمیشہ کسی جماعت کے منشور یا پروگرام کو دیکھ کر دینا چاہیئے۔ جب اکثریتی جماعت حکومت بناتی ہے تو پھر اپنے وعدوں اور منشور کو عملی شکل دینے کیلئے قانون سازی کرتی ہے۔ مسائل کو حل کرنے کیلئے پارٹی اپنی تجاویز کو قانون میں تبدیل کرتی ہے۔ ترقی یافتہ دُنیا میں یہی طریقہ ہوتا ہے جس کی وجہ سے وہاں کے سیاسی نظام مستحکم ہوتے ہیں۔ ہمارا مسئلہ یہ ہے کہ جماعتیں برسرِ اقتدار آ کر اپنے منشور اور پروگرام نظر انداز کرتی ہیں اور ایک منفی سیاسی ثقافت وجود پذیر ہو جاتی ہے۔ نتیجہ یہ ہوتا ہے کہ ہمارا سیاسی نظام غیر مستحکم رہتا ہے۔

… observe the leadership and test its character, and then allocate a place for that party in national politics. People note every word of the leader and comment on it. In any political party the most important posts are those of chairman, president, general secretary, press secretary, finance secretary etc. Among them there is a regular distribution of powers.

If political parties have been made on the basis of principles and rules, then these parties prove to be the spirit of democracy. Their thinking is constructive and creative. They see the distribution of powers in the constitution in the light of national interests. These same parties become the cause of the development of party unity and have belief or confidence in the importance of the electoral system, which proves to be the forerunner of a successful political system.

Government of a Political Party and its Performance in the light of its Manifesto

A necessary element of every political party is the party’s manifesto (Charter/Manifesto). Every political party, identifying the important problems of the country, compiles a programme or proposals to solve those problems, which is called a manifesto. In the light of this same manifesto, in the form of political and electoral promises, parties take part in elections. When the majority of the public agree with these promises and programmes, that party, winning the elections (obtaining the public mandate), forms the government. Here it is worth mentioning that the vote should always be given by looking at the manifesto or programme of a party. When the majority party forms the government, it then makes laws to give practical form to its promises and manifesto. To solve problems the party changes its proposals into law. In the developed world this is the method, because of which the political systems there are stable. Our problem is that parties, on coming into power, ignore their manifesto and programme, and a negative political culture comes into being. The result is that our political system remains unstable.
